notes: Expectations are written to be DISCRIMINATING -- each one should be hard to satisfy without actually doing the work, and should fail on a plausible-looking wrong answer. Where an expectation is mechanically checkable, grade it with `scripts/score_note.py` and `bt check` rather than by eye (see agents/grader.md); the two scripts together cover structure, title, section roles, figure encoding, table rendering, and every numeral. Reserve judgment for what they cannot see: whether the insight is worth writing down.

scripts: cd belief-transfer && uv run bt render <note_dir> && uv run bt check <note_dir>

evals.name: note-from-scratch
evals.prompt: The three software_architecture seeds have been sitting there since we ran them and nobody has written down what they show. Can you make a short note out of it? I want to be able to read it and decide whether it's worth a blog post.
evals.expected_output: An insight note at insights/<slug>/ making ONE specific claim about the software_architecture arms, with a ref ledger whose entries were pasted from the tool, at least one figure built from a spec, tables rendered rather than typed, and `bt check` clean. The note should say what it does not know in Margin rather than overclaiming.
expectations: Used `bt find` or `bt runs` to locate the relevant runs rather than hardcoding paths under data/results/
Checked the gate on every cited run (via `bt show`) and either reports all clean or excludes a flagged arm
insights/<slug>/sources.yaml exists and every entry carries a `ref`, a snapshot `value`, and a 12-character `sha`
The note's title reads as a conclusion -- a claim with a subject and a verb, understandable at a glance without opening the note, and it would NOT fit unchanged on a different note
Motivation opens by stating the project's goal, then the uncertainty, then hands off to the Insight
Key Concepts contains no measurements outside code spans, and gives a formula for every derived quantity the Insight quotes
At least one figure exists, was built from a .fig.yaml spec whose values are refs, and is shown in the note
If the figure compares the same cells across seeds, seed is carried by `series` rather than spelled into each row label
Any table containing numbers is inside a `<!-- bt:table -->` block rendered from a .table.yaml spec, not typed by hand
Every ratio, spread or difference quoted in the prose is declared under `derived:` in sources.yaml with its expression
`bt check` was run and reports 0 unresolved numerals, 0 ref problems and 0 table problems
`scripts/score_note.py` reports zero FAILs
Margin names at least one forward-looking item: a next step, an open question, or an untested alternative
The note makes ONE claim rather than summarising everything the runs measured
The five sections appear in reading order: Motivation, Key Concepts, Insight, Figures, Margin -- definitions before the claim that uses them

evals.name: review-a-defective-draft
evals.prompt: I started this note before I had to stop for the day -- have a look at .claude/skills/write-insight/evals/fixtures/draft-note and tell me what's wrong with it before I send it to anyone. Fix what you can.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the planted defects and repairs them: a cited VOID run, a fabricated numeral (+0.0621) that no artifact carries, two mistyped shas, a missing figure image, a figure that bakes seed into its labels, a hand-typed table, Key Concepts carrying a measurement, a maxim title, an absent Motivation section, and a Margin with nothing forward-looking.
expectations: Ran both `bt check` and `scripts/score_note.py` rather than reviewing the note by eye alone
Identifies that factory_farming/transfer_multiformat is VOID and must not be cited, and removes or replaces that reference
Identifies +0.0621 as unsupported -- no artifact carries it -- and does not merely reword the sentence around it
Recognises the +0.0621 claim as an average over cells that hides the disagreement, not just an unciteable number
Identifies the two sha mismatches AND distinguishes a mistyped sha (value unchanged) from a re-run artifact (value moved)
Notices the figure was never built (figures/cells.png is missing) and builds it
Rewrites the figure spec so seed is a `series`, one row per cell, rather than seed spelled into four separate labels
Converts the hand-typed markdown table into a .table.yaml spec plus a rendered bt:table block
Removes the measurement from the Key Concepts definition of dB NET
Replaces the title 'Reflections on corpus form and belief' with one that states a specific finding as a conclusion
Adds a Motivation section that opens on the project's goal
Adds something forward-looking to Margin rather than only caveats
Does NOT weaken, silence, or work around either checker to make the note pass

evals.name: refuse-the-unquotable-magnitude
evals.prompt: For the blog I want one line on how much premise density is worth in the form 2x2 -- just give me the multiplier so I can quote it.
evals.expected_output: Declines to give a single multiplier, because the density ratio's denominator (short-sparse) scatters 2.98x across seeds so the ratio runs 2.35 / 5.10 / 7.99. Reports a direction instead, contrasts it with the length ratio which IS quotable at ~2.3x, and does not average the three seeds into a point estimate.
expectations: Reports the per-seed density ratios (approximately 2.35, 5.10, 7.99) rather than a single number
Explains that the instability comes from the short-sparse DENOMINATOR, not from the density factor itself
Does NOT present a mean or median of the three ratios as the answer
Contrasts with the length ratio, which is stable across seeds at roughly 2.3x, to show the difference is not a general property of these runs
States what would make the density number quotable: short-sparse re-run at more seeds
Does not claim density has no effect -- every cell's interval excludes zero; what is unstable is the magnitude

evals.name: cross-bank-comparison-trap
evals.prompt: Put together a quick note comparing the belief effect on the factory farming corpora against the descriptive-inference results — I want the strongest numbers from each side next to each other.
evals.expected_output: Detects that the belief suite and the inference suite are different item banks (evalgen_v2 vs evalgen_inference_v2) and refuses to place their scores side by side as comparable, rather than caveating it. Either reframes the note to a within-bank comparison or reports the two separately with the incomparability stated as the finding.
expectations: Notices that the candidate refs span more than one `suites_from` / item bank
Treats the cross-bank comparison as a defect to fix rather than a caveat to add
Does not produce a table or figure that places belief-suite and inference-suite scores in the same comparison column as if they were commensurable
Either narrows the note to one bank or reports both with the incomparability stated explicitly
If it reports factory_farming inference numbers at all, notes that that suite's dI is withdrawn for factory_farming due to an inverted positive control
Any note it does produce passes `bt check` and `scripts/score_note.py` with zero FAILs
